issue_title: fix(seo): give public schedules event-specific metadata and canonical URLs
problem_statement:
fix(seo): give public schedules event-specific metadata and canonical URLs

Observed during the owner-requested schedule track-description/AEO verification on 2026-09-14, at ATA release c2a5565444cf48790cb3d5fa9589e5f59b5810ca:

`https://events.allthingsai.org/events/all-things-ai-2026/schedule` returns HTTP 200 with the correct title and server-rendered schedule. Its initial HTML uses the generic site meta description (“The community for AI practitioners and users — news, events, and insights delivered to your inbox.”), has no canonical link, and includes no JSON-LD. Lighthouse 13.4.1 nevertheless scores SEO 100; that score does not cover all AEO/metadata requirements.

Source: `src/app/(public)/events/[eventSlug]/schedule/page.tsx` currently returns only `title` from `generateMetadata`. This predates #2030 and is independent of public track-description rendering. Existing issue search found no bounded schedule-metadata issue; #1348 is a launch-control epic, not an implementation lane.

Bounded follow-up:

- Give the public schedule event-specific description and canonical metadata using the existing public-origin resolution and event visibility rules.
- Assess whether the schedule should reuse existing structured-data helpers for event/breadcrumb context; use verified event data only and avoid redundant or contradictory entities.
- Add assertions on the actual server HTML, including custom-domain versus default-domain behavior and draft/unpublished schedules. Preserve the current no-draft-content boundary.
- Re-run Lighthouse and a separate metadata/AEO check. Do not claim that structured data guarantees ranking or inclusion in AI answers.

No schema, event data, provider, secret, or deployment-setting changes are requested by this issue. This is a newly observed product gap, not an additional gate on #2030.
